subject: P99 connection-establish spikes impacting Omnichat - urgent
messages:
From: Ben Lee <ben@omnichat.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes — connection establish times up 3x since 09:00 PST

Laura / Redwood support,

We started seeing a broad spike in request latency this morning around 09:00 PST. Our application is spiking at p95/p99 for "time-to-first-token" equivalent (we measure TTFB at our edge) — p99 is ~3x baseline and some requests are timing out (35s). The errors are mostly 525/524 from our CDN and we see repeated TLS handshake stalls in the traces. This started coincident with what I assume is normal traffic growth, but the shape looks like a handshake/connection establishment regression rather than model-side token generation.

I've attached a small trace sample (omnichat_ttft_traces_2027-01-22.zip) and we'll forward anything else helpful. This is affecting a handful of enterprise customers tonight; we're getting pressure from our execs. Can you confirm receipt and a plan for next steps?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Lee
CTO, Omnichat

Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spikes — connection establish times up 3x since 09:00 PST

Quick update from investigation:
- Correlation: spike onset ~09:03 PST, aligns with elevated SYN retransmits between CDN edges and our origin pool for the hosted API.
- Symptom: majority of affected requests show prolonged TLS handshake (ClientHello -> ServerHello delay) and repeated TCP retransmits before handshake completes. Not seeing model CPU/GPU queuing anomalies.
- Hypothesis: upstream CDN edge has tightened connection timeouts / a config push increased TLS session renegotiation frequency, causing extra round trips for cold connections.
- Evidence: packet-level traces show extra 100–250ms per handshake on affected flows; curl-based handshake tests to the affected POP show elevated RTT compared to baseline.

Immediate remediation I recommend:
1) Push sticky routing for Omnichat flows to a smaller subset of healthy edges (reduce cross-edge hairpin).
2) Enable connection keepalive and TLS session resumption hints on the ingress layer for 1 hour.
3) Route Omnichat to a dedicated instance pool (briefly) to remove variability from multi-tenant connection churn.

I’m running a live trace now and will paste results into the Jira ticket. If we get sign-off we can deploy the route change within ~20 minutes.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
